narrative:
The Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 44.8% on November 11, 2026, taking up 1,275 of the 2,845 scheduled matters across 54 judges. This represents an improvement compared to prior recorded sessions earlier in the month, which logged hearing rates of 35.6% on November 5, 40.5% on November 4, and 30.1% on November 3. 

Performance across court halls showed substantial variation. Justice V. Srishananda (Hall 23) achieved an efficient 78.8% clearance rate across 80 scheduled matters, hearing 63 cases. Similarly, the bench of Justice Jayant Banerji and Justice N.V. Bhavani (Hall 3) heard 37 of 51 matters (72.5%) in its primary roster, alongside solid clearance in smaller supplementary lists. Conversely, high-volume dockets faced bottlenecks; Justice R. Nataraj (Hall 16) heard 65 of 172 scheduled cases (37.8%), Justice Hanchate Sanjeevkumar (Hall 24) heard 28 of 110 matters (25.5%), and Hall 30 under Justice S. Rachaiah heard none of its 84 scheduled cases.

Procedural stages heavily dictated throughput. Matters listed for Orders constituted the largest operational volume, with 525 of 1,023 cases heard (51.3%), reflecting stronger conversion than the 31.9% observed on November 5. Preliminary Hearings converted at 52.3% (192 heard of 367 scheduled), while Admission matters saw 293 hearings out of 707 (41.4%). Final Hearing stages continued to experience slower clearance, converting just 21.1% (107 heard of 507 scheduled), consistent with historical trends of 20.8% to 29.4%.

Writ Petitions (WP) dominated the subject-matter workload with 1,253 scheduled listings and 565 heard (45.1%), marking a higher clearance rate than the 31.4% to 37.0% seen earlier in November. Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) followed with a 53.9% hearing rate (241 heard of 447), while Criminal Appeals (CRL.A) recorded 65.0% (102 of 157). Lower clearance persisted in civil appeals, with Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) reaching 33.2% and Regular First Appeals (RFA) converting at 23.0%.
